answer:
The OSHA PSM threshold quantity for chlorine (CAS 7782-50-5) is 1,500 lb. That figure comes from the current eCFR text of 29 CFR 1910.119, Appendix A ("List of Highly Hazardous Chemicals, Toxics and Reactives"), which I fetched and checked.

- The 1,500 lb is the most that can sit in a process at any one time. If a process holds that much or more, the PSM standard applies.
- Chlorine dioxide, chlorine pentafluoride and chlorine trifluoride are separate entries in Appendix A, each with its own threshold. I did not pull their values.
- This answers only the OSHA question. Other programs set their own chlorine thresholds; for example, EPA RMP (40 CFR 68) uses 2,500 lb. I did not check that figure in this session.
